description: On a `tg --tag decision …` / `tg --tag problem …` send, runs the decision-request-discipline self-check: parses (shlex, not raw-match) the message body and grades it against the structural markers (Context / Options / Recommendation). Graduated verdict, lenient by design: a complete body passes silently; a partial body gets an exit-0 ADVISORY naming what's absent; only a genuinely BARE body (no table, none of the markers) is BLOCKED (exit 10) with the re-send skeleton. The removed `question` tag (agent-tools#524 / tg-cli#301: an open question is a decision request) is BLOCKED outright with a one-line redirect to --tag decision, no hatch. on_error=open: a crash must never wedge the human's channel. There is NO self-service escape (the old ALLOW_RAW_DECISION_REQUEST env and `# decision-request-ok:` sentinel are removed); a one-time force-through of a BARE body is an external Telegram approval requested via RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_DECISION_REQUEST_FORMAT="<why>" (deny-by-default; only exit 0 lets it through). timeout_ms 960000 exceeds the hatch helper's 930s worst case (tg-ctl ask's 900s cap plus a 30s cleanup margin) so the request can actually reach a human before the bridge's descriptor-timeout kill. Claude Code settings entries that launch cc_hook_bridge must also set timeout >960s. The common env-unset deny path may make ONE bounded daemon-local grant pull (tg-ctl ask --verify-grant --pull, agent-tools#742; ~20s worst case: 15s lookup cap + a git rev-parse for repoRoot) before denying, once per (hook, cwd) per process — fail-closed, no Telegram card.
